After 8 years and 10 billion km, a pioneering X-ray telescope captured its first observations, revealing better performance than expected. item.title: There's an impostor hiding in the Hyades star cluster. Can you spot it?
item.description:
【AI 精简版】 AI-condensed version. This text was produced by an LLM from the original article and may omit details. The original link at the end is the only authoritative source.

Why it is here: Educational piece on star clusters with clear reporting and useful vocabulary.

Aldebaran, the brightest star in the Hyades cluster, is actually a foreground star 65 light-years away, while the Hyades are 150 light-years distant. This reveals the night sky's depth and the illusion of constellations. The Hyades is an open cluster 153 light-years from Earth, while Aldebaran is a separate star.

Source: Space.com | Published: 2026-11-20 19:00 UTC
